name: Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai)
short: The 12 m golden Buddha on Koh Fan islet, Samui's best-known landmark, 3 km from the airport.

name: Wat Plai Laem
short: Colourful lakeside temple with an 18-armed Guanyin and a laughing Buddha, 1 km from Big Buddha.

name: Hin Ta and Hin Yai (Grandfather and Grandmother Rocks)
short: The famous rock formations at the south end of Lamai, with a lane of snack and souvenir stalls.

name: Na Muang Waterfall 1
short: The island's best-known waterfall with a swimmable pool; thin to a trickle February–April.

name: Na Muang Waterfall 2
short: A 20–40 minute steep climb with ropes above Na Muang 1; busy by 10:30.

name: Hin Lad Waterfall
short: Jungle waterfall 2 km inland from Nathon, about two hours round trip on a steep trail.

name: Wat Khunaram (mummified monk)
short: Home of the mummified monk Luang Pho Daeng, seated in a glass case; cover shoulders and knees.

name: Secret Buddha Garden (Tarnim Magic Garden)
short: Hillside sculpture garden in the central highlands; very steep road, best by 4x4 or on a tour.

name: Overlap Stone
short: Balanced boulders and a suspension bridge above Lamai, with wide views; steep access road.

name: Lad Koh Viewpoint
short: Ring-road pull-off between Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove; stay off the rocks when waves are up.

name: Fisherman's Village, Bophut
short: Old wooden shophouses, Samui's best restaurant street and the Friday walking street.

name: Wat Ratchathammaram (Red Temple, Wat Sila Ngu)
short: Terracotta-red temple covered in carved reliefs on the ring road between Lamai and Hua Thanon.

name: Laem Sor Pagoda
short: Gold-tiled seafront chedi on the quiet south coast near Bang Kao.

name: Guan Yu Shrine, Hua Thanon
short: A 16 m bronze statue of the Chinese general Guan Yu on the hillside above Hua Thanon.

name: Hua Thanon fishing village
short: Muslim fishing community with a morning fish market and Samui's central mosque.

name: Chaweng
short: Samui's main beach and resort strip: 7 km of white sand, the most restaurants, bars and shops.
swim: Good; red flags and rip currents October–December

name: Chaweng Noi
short: Quiet cove south of Chaweng with coarser sand and snorkelling off the beach.

name: Lamai
short: The second beach: 4 km of sand with a slower pace than Chaweng, night market and value stays.
swim: Centre is best but drops steeply; north end stony; rough October–December

name: Silver Beach (Crystal Bay)
short: Small boulder-framed cove with pale sand and clear water; fills by 10:00.

name: Coral Cove
short: Rocky cove for snorkelling; coarse sand, so wear water shoes.

name: Choeng Mon
short: Sheltered north-east bay with soft white sand and a sandbar to Koh Fan Noi at low tide; 5–10 min from the airport.
swim: Among the calmest on the island

name: Tongson Bay
short: Small sheltered bay reached by a sand track; clear and shallow December–April.
swim: Clear and shallow Dec–Apr; rougher May–Oct

name: Bang Rak (Big Buddha Beach)
short: The pier beach next to the airport: ferries to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, seafood on the sand, not for swimming.

name: Bophut Beach
short: The beach in front of Fisherman's Village; good for dinner on the sand, not for swimming.
swim: Not recommended: cloudy water, jellyfish reported

name: Maenam
short: Long, quiet palm-lined beach on the north coast with the Lomprayah pier and cheap long stays.
swim: Calm in the dry season; chest-deep about 5 m out

name: Bang Por
short: Quiet north-west beach known for seafood restaurants and sunsets; swim at high tide only.
swim: High tide only; stony flat at low tide [check: sources conflict]

name: Laem Yai
short: Very quiet north-west beach, partly resort frontage, with snorkelling and sunsets.
swim: Poor at low tide; clear water for snorkelling

name: Nathon
short: The original capital and main ferry port on the west coast: government offices, old shophouses, a daily night market and sunsets from the pier. [GPS: take from Google Maps]

name: Lipa Noi
short: Quiet west-coast beach with very shallow calm water; the Raja ferry pier and Nikki Beach are nearby.
swim: Very shallow and calm; wide flats at low tide

name: Taling Ngam
short: Long quiet village beach with fishing boats and the island's best sunset over the Five Islands.

name: Thong Krut
short: South-west pier village where the Pig Island and Koh Tan boats leave. [GPS: take from Google Maps]

name: Bang Kao
short: Quiet south-coast beach with few facilities; swim at high tide, water shoes for coral pieces.

name: Koh Madsum (Pig Island)
short: The small island with the beach pigs, 15–30 minutes by boat from Thong Krut; usually paired with Koh Tan. [GPS: take from Google Maps]

name: Koh Tan
short: Quiet island with the best shallow reef snorkelling near Samui and a couple of beach restaurants. [GPS: take from Google Maps]

name: Mu Ko Ang Thong National Marine Park
area: Gulf of Thailand, ~30 km west of Samui
short: 42 limestone islands with the Emerald Lake, viewpoints and reefs; HQ on Koh Wua Talab. Closed every year 1 November–15 December. [GPS: approximate, verify]

name: Samui International Airport (USM)
short: Open-air airport run by Bangkok Airways; 20–25 flights a day to Bangkok plus Singapore, Hong Kong, Phuket, Chiang Mai. [GPS: verify]

name: Bangkok Hospital Samui
short: Private hospital on the ring road near Chaweng Noi with trauma and paediatric units; hotline 1719. [GPS and phone: verify on the hospital's own site]

name: Koh Samui Hospital (government)
short: The government hospital on the outskirts of Nathon. [GPS and phone: verify]

name: Koh Samui Immigration Office
short: 333 Maenam Road, Soi 1, Moo 1, Maenam 84330 (moved from Nathon in 2016). Extensions, 90-day reports, TM30. [GPS: take from Google Maps]

name: Koh Samui Tourist Police
short: Tourist Police hotline 1155; local office +66 77 430 018 [check location]. Police 191, ambulance 1669, fire 199.
